issues.description: The UML in the problem statement defines Animal with a constructor Animal(String, int) (name and age), but the provided solution implements Animal with a single-argument constructor Animal(String). The template's Main also creates animals using single-argument constructors (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle")). This mismatch between the UML/specification and the template/solution will confuse students about the expected constructor signature for Animal and its subclasses.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification, template, and solution consistent. Either update the UML/problem statement to require Animal(String) (remove age) or update the template and solution to implement Animal(String, int) and adjust all subclasses and example usages (e.g., Main) to pass both name and age. Ensure constructors across Animal and its subclasses match the chosen signature.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares an 'age: int' attribute for Animal, but the solution's Animal class does not declare an age attribute at all (only a name field). This absence of the age attribute contradicts the UML and the textual parts that reference initializing all class attributes, and will confuse students about whether Animal should include age.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify whether Animal should have an 'age' attribute. If yes, add a private int age field to Animal, update its constructor to accept and initialize age, add getter/setter for age, and update all subclasses and example usages (Main and tests) to provide age. If no, remove the age entry from the UML and any textual references so the specification matches the template and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) specifies that Animal has two attributes (name and age) and a constructor Animal(String, int), but the provided implementation (solution and template usage) uses a single-argument constructor Animal(String) and subclasses' constructors that accept only a name. This creates a mismatch in the conceptual entity 'Animal' across artifacts: the parameter/attribute 'age' referenced in the problem is missing from the code, so students cannot reliably map the UML/requirements to the template/solution implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the representations consistent. Either (A) update the code to match the UML: add an 'age' attribute with getter/setter and change Animal and all subclass constructors to accept (String name, int age) and pass age to super, or (B) update the problem statement/UML to require only a name (Animal(String)) and remove 'age' from the UML and constructor signature. Choose the option that preserves the intended learning objective.
